newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Gunman attacks Argentine ex-first lady's lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Gunman attacks Argentine ex-first lady's lawyer.

text.p: A lawyer representing President Carlos Menem's ex-wife Zulema Yoma in her effort to prove their son's death in a helicopter crash in 1995 was no accident, said on Tuesday he had been shot at and threatened.

Mario Rotundo said a car pulled up beside his vehicle in Buenos Aires on Monday night and a man shot at him three times. "But when I saw the gun out of the corner of my eye I reacted and managed to accelerate," he said.
Rotundo, who escaped unhurt, told reporters he then got a message on his telephone answering machine saying: "This time it was a warning, next time you're a dead man if you don't drop this case."
Carlos "Carlitos" Menem Jr. died in March 1995 at age 26 when the helicopter he was piloting crashed. A close friend who was flying with him also died.

The air force said they were flying low above a highway and hit a cable, but Yoma believes her son was a victim of a murky plot involving drugs and officials in the Casa Rosada government palace. She had her son's body exhumed for a second autopsy and says an ex-secret service man told her there was a third person, a mysterious blonde, in the doomed helicopter.

News reports last week said a study of the wreckage by the Gendarme border police turned up evidence that the helicopter was hit by bullets. The Gendarmes did not deny the report but said the study had not been completed.

Officials dismiss the former first lady as hysterical but her conspiracy theory is gaining space in the media. She said in a television interview on Monday that her ex-husband "never denied to me" their son may have been killed.
Menem, who also had a daughter with Yoma, often refers to the pain of losing his son but says Yoma's theory is the product of a mother's understandable grief.

Yoma said in Monday's interview that shortly before her son died, "he named a person to me, someone very close to government house, who might make an attempt on his life." She said it would be "imprudent" to name that person yet.

Another of Yoma's lawyers, Ignacio Irrurzum, said the attack on Rotundo "is obviously linked with the murder of her son. All of us who are investigating the murder are the victims of constant threats."
